stories.headline: Anthropic signs $35B cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda for a Texas data center

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed a cloud-computing deal worth $35 billion with Lambda, a San Jose cloud provider backed by Nvidia, for a Texas data center, sources said on Monday, Aug. 31, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has signed a cloud-computing deal worth US$35 billion with Lambda, a cloud provider backed by Nvidia, for a Texas data centre, a source familiar with the matter said on Monday (Aug 31).

key_facts.fact: The project is in Nueces County, Texas, developed by crypto-miner-turned-AI-data-center company Hut 8, and covers about 350 megawatts of capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: The project is being developed in Nueces County by crypto-mining-turned-AI data centre company Hut 8 and covers a capacity of about 350 megawatts, the source said.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal, which first reported the deal, said Nvidia itself would hold the lease on the data center — Nvidia has invested in both Anthropic and Lambda and supplies the chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia, which has invested in both Anthropic and Lambda, will lease the data center from Hut 8, and Lambda will then pay Nvidia an unknown amount to get access to the data center, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The agreement with Lambda runs six years, according to a source familiar with the deal.
key_facts.excerpt: The San Francisco-based AI lab has agreed to a six-year deal with Lambda, a source familiar with the deal told AFP.

key_facts.fact: Hut 8 said in July it had signed a 15-year lease with an 'investment-grade customer' with a base-term contract value of $19.6 billion; the FT later reported Nvidia was the tenant for Hut 8's 1-gigawatt Beacon Point campus.
key_facts.excerpt: Hut 8 said in July it had signed a lease deal with an "investment-grade customer" for 15 years, with a base-term contract value of US$19.6 billion. The Financial Times later reported that Nvidia was the tenant for Hut 8's 1-gigawatt Beacon Point campus.

key_facts.fact: The deal follows a string of Anthropic compute commitments: $45 billion with Nscale in West Virginia on Aug. 26, $50 billion with Fluidstack and $45 billion with SpaceX in recent months.
key_facts.excerpt: The Claude chatbot maker on Aug 26 agreed to spend US$45 billion to rent capacity from Nscale in West Virginia. In recent months, it has also signed cloud deals for US$50 billion with neocloud Fluidstack and US$45 billion with Elon Musk's SpaceX.

stories.headline: AMD and Cisco switch on Saudi AI compute with Humain, plan 250MW MI400 phase from 2027

key_facts.fact: AMD, Cisco and HUMAIN announced on Aug. 31, 2026 that AI infrastructure built on AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs and Cisco Silicon One networking is now live in Saudi Arabia and serving HUMAIN customers.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD (NASDAQ: AMD), Cisco (NASDAQ: CSCO) and HUMAIN, a PIF company delivering full-stack AI solutions, today announced that AMD Instinct MI355X GPU-based AI infrastructure built on Cisco Silicon One-based AI networking is now live in Saudi Arabia and serving HUMAIN customers in the Kingdom and beyond.

key_facts.fact: The deployment pairs AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs with AMD EPYC CPUs, interconnected by Cisco's N9000 Series platform built on Cisco Silicon One and 800G optics, letting HUMAIN offer GPU-as-a-service for training and inference.
key_facts.excerpt: Built on Cisco Silicon One and Cisco 800G optics, the Cisco N9000 Series platform interconnects the MI355X GPUs in an AI-optimized fabric designed for scale, low latency and operational resilience, enabling HUMAIN to offer GPU-as-a-service across a wide range of use cases, from model training to inferencing.

key_facts.fact: The three companies plan a next phase of up to 250 megawatts using AMD Instinct MI400 Series GPUs, with deployment starting in 2027 and capacity coming online in the second half of that year.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD, Cisco and HUMAIN plan to deploy up to 250 megawatts of AI infrastructure powered by AMD Instinct MI400 Series GPUs, AMD EPYC CPUs and AMD ROCm open software... Deployment is planned to begin in 2027, with capacity expected to start coming online in the second half of the year.

key_facts.fact: The joint venture remains on track to deploy up to 1 gigawatt of AI infrastructure in Saudi Arabia by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Driven by strong customer demand, the joint venture remains on track to deploy up to 1 gigawatt of AI infrastructure by 2030.

stories.headline: Trump says communities rejecting data centers want to be 'backwards and poor'

key_facts.fact: In a Truth Social post on Monday, Aug. 31, 2026, Trump wrote that 'the only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor' and urged them to 'let Data Reign.'
key_facts.excerpt: Posting on his Truth Social platform, the President said that communities that reject data centers only do so because "they want to end up being backwards and poor"... The President says to "let Data Reign" if communities "want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place."

key_facts.fact: Trump added: 'If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame. China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement. Actually, they can't believe it is happening!'
key_facts.excerpt: "If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame. China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement. Actually, they can't believe it is happening!" wrote Trump

key_facts.fact: Vice President JD Vance, asked about the post the same day at Joint Base Andrews, said 'probably 99 percent of the backlash to data centers has come in areas where building a data center means higher utility and higher electricity' and argued builders 'should be putting power back into the grid, not taking it out.'
key_facts.excerpt: "I think probably 99 percent of the backlash to data centers has come in areas where building a data center means higher utility and higher electricity for the people on the ground," Vice President JD Vance told reporters Monday at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland... "If you build the data center, you should be putting power back into the grid, not taking it out," he added

key_facts.fact: Pew polling cited by Gizmodo found 71% of Americans oppose data center construction in their community, making them less popular than nuclear plants.
key_facts.excerpt: A whopping 71% of Americans oppose data center construction in their community, according to Pew Research, making them even less popular than building nuclear power plants in a community.

key_facts.fact: Local bans on data center developments crossed 500 nationwide last month; Texas Gov. Greg Abbott in early August cut new data centers off from grid connections pending an ERCOT/PUCT audit, and New York issued a one-year moratorium in July.
key_facts.excerpt: And last month, the number of local bans on data center developments crossed over 500 within the United States... In July, New York Governor Cathy Hochul signed a one-year moratorium on data center construction... In early August, Texas Governor Greg Abbott directed state agencies to cut data centers off from connecting to the Texas power grid until an audit of the facility's power and water usage is completed.

key_facts.fact: A July Georgia Tech study found data centers raise local employment 3.5%, wages 5% and median household income 1.9%, but with 'negligible' benefits in rural areas and electricity prices up an average 5% after a data center is built.
key_facts.excerpt: A July study from Georgia Tech found that data center developments increase local employment by 3.5%, total wages by 5%, business establishments by 4.7%, and median household income by 1.9%... the study found that these benefits mainly show up in metropolitan areas, calling the benefits in rural areas "negligible."... finding that prices rise an average of 5% after a data center is built in a community.

stories.headline: Google raises US prices on TV Streamer and Nest cameras, blaming rising component costs

key_facts.fact: Google raised the price of the Google TV Streamer from $99.99 to $149.99 in the US — a $50 increase on a device that launched in 2024 — with the new price live on the Google Store and Best Buy as of Monday, Aug. 31, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has quietly raised the price of the Google TV Streamer to $149.99. This $50 increase is quite drastic for the 2024 Google TV device that launched at $99.99 and saw $20 discounts during the holidays. This new price is already live on the Google Store and Best Buy, but other retailers (like Amazon) are still selling it at the original price as of Monday afternoon.

key_facts.fact: Google said in a statement: 'Due to rising component costs, we are adjusting the U.S. pricing of select Google Nest cameras, doorbells and Google TV streamer 4K, effective August 31.'
key_facts.excerpt: Google shared the following statement with 9to5 today: Due to rising component costs, we are adjusting the U.S. pricing of select Google Nest cameras, doorbells and Google TV streamer 4K, effective August 31.

key_facts.fact: 9to5Google attributes the increase to RAM pricing — the streamer carries 4GB of RAM and 32GB of storage — noting the Pixel 11 series and Pixel Watch 5 already reflect the new memory reality.
key_facts.excerpt: This increase is presumably due to RAM pricing, with the Pixel 11 series and Pixel Watch 5 already reflecting this new reality. The Google TV Streamer has 4 GB of RAM and 32 GB of storage.

key_facts.fact: Memory supply is tightening as AI data-center demand pulls capacity toward HBM: Samsung is reported to have committed up to 70% of its memory production to long-term agreements through 2031, and Reuters reported Samsung expects chip shortages to become more acute and extend into 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: SamMobile reports that Samsung has allocated up to 70% of memory production capacity to long-term agreements through 2031... Reuters reported that Samsung expects global chip shortages to become more acute and extend into 2028.

stories.headline: SPAC-bound ONE Nuclear locks site for 2.88GW Louisiana plant with co-located data center campus

key_facts.fact: ONE Nuclear Energy announced on Aug. 31, 2026 that it executed a binding letter of intent with a Louisiana landowner group giving it site control for Project Cayman.
key_facts.excerpt: ONE Nuclear Energy LLC ("ONE Nuclear"), an independent developer of large-scale energy solutions powered by natural gas and advanced nuclear technologies, announced today that it has executed a binding letter of intent (LOI) with a prominent Louisiana landowner group, providing site control for the development of Project Cayman

key_facts.fact: Project Cayman is a 2.88 GW natural gas plant plus a 700MW / 2.88GWh battery energy storage system, with a co-located high-capacity data center campus.
key_facts.excerpt: Project Cayman, a 2.88 GW natural gas plant and a 700MW, 2.88GWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project with a co-located high-capacity data center campus.

key_facts.fact: ONE Nuclear CEO Richard Taylor said the project 'will deliver the reliable energy needed to support new investment, create jobs, expand the local tax base and generate additional funding for community priorities and critical infrastructure.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Project Cayman, with its 2.88 GW power capacity, demonstrates that ONE Nuclear is committed to supporting the future economic development of one of Louisiana's most important industrial regions," said Richard Taylor, CEO of ONE Nuclear.

key_facts.fact: Hennessy Capital Investment Corp. VII shareholders approved ONE Nuclear's business combination on Aug. 24, 2026; the combined company is expected to list under the ticker 'ONEN' after a close anticipated in the second half of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: On August 24, 2026, ONE Nuclear's previously announced business combination (the "Business Combination") with Hennessy Capital Investment Corp. VII (NASDAQ: HVII) ("Hennessy VII") was approved by the Hennessy VII shareholders. The combined company is expected to be listed on a national exchange under the ticker symbol "ONEN" following an anticipated transaction close in the second half of 2026

key_facts.fact: HVII shares rose 5.76% on the Aug. 31 announcement, after a 12.48% gain on the Aug. 25 shareholder-approval news.
